testing_framework.null_hypothesis: H_0: R_cand - R_base <= -delta (Candidate recall is inferior by >= delta)
testing_framework.alternative_hypothesis: H_1: R_cand - R_base > -delta (Candidate recall is non-inferior within margin delta)
testing_framework.test_statistic: Z = ( (R_cand - R_base) + delta ) / sqrt( (p_disc - d^2) / N_D )

formula_A_lan_demets_sfldof.formula_expression: alpha*(t) = 2 - 2 * Phi( Z_{1 - alpha/2} / sqrt(t) ) = 2 * (1 - Phi( 1.95996 / sqrt(t) ))
formula_A_lan_demets_sfldof.mathematical_rationale: Why Z_{0.025} = 1.95996 is used: Lan & DeMets (1983) constructed the O'Brien-Fleming spending function from Brownian motion exit across symmetric barriers, incorporating a factor of 2 based on the reflection principle. When calibrating this function to spend a total alpha = 0.05 at horizon t=1, the argument must evaluate to Phi^{-1}(1 - alpha/2) = 1.95996 so that 2 * (1 - 0.975) = 0.0500. If one naively substituted Z_{0.05} = 1.64485 into 2 - 2*Phi(...), the function would evaluate to 2 * (1 - 0.95) = 0.1000 at t=1, spending twice the permitted Type I error budget.

historical_discrepancy_audit.root_cause_of_discrepancy: The previous values [2.96, 2.14, 1.71] were an uncalibrated hybrid: Z_1=2.96 and Z_3=1.71 were taken from discrete O'Brien-Fleming (where Z_k = 1.71 / sqrt(t_k)), while Z_2=2.14 was taken from Lan-DeMets spending. At Look 1, Z_1=2.96 had a nominal p-value of 0.0015, which exceeded the Lan-DeMets Look 1 alpha budget of 0.000687 by more than a factor of 2! Under the rigorously solved Lan-DeMets design, Z_1 MUST be 3.1993 (~3.20) to strictly restrict Look 1 alpha to 0.000687.
